<!-- Use this template for one connected family of ideas.
Choose a home in mathematics/, machine-learning/, robotics/, physics/,
computer-hardware/, or computer-software/.
Place electrical engineering material directly in physics/.
Use lowercase, hyphen-separated filenames that name the family.
Give related concepts sections within the same document when they form one explanation.
Keep a separate supporting note when it has substantial reusable material.
Use categories and cross-links for relationships that cross folder boundaries.
Keep one sentence per line and use level-two headings for sections.
Leave definitions, assumptions, and main results visible.
Place supporting calculations in a closed callout immediately after the result.
Use Derivation for a calculation and Proof for an argument establishing a claim.
Keep the full explanation in one main note and link to its sections from related notes.
Include a short definition or result locally when a reader needs it to follow the argument.
Do not force the reader to leave the page for every prerequisite reminder.
Use the reading route why -> what -> how -> use -> relationships.
These headings are a guide, not a requirement to repeat six headings for every family member.
Combine short sections and give substantial family members descriptive level-two headings.
Distinguish a definition, theorem, modelling assumption, approximation, and empirical claim.
Remove unused sections and replace the metadata placeholders before publishing.
-->

## Definition and meaning {#definition}

<!-- What kind of thing is the concept: function, distribution, property, procedure, or relationship?
Give its precise definition, then interpret each important clause in plain language.
State its inputs, outputs, domains, units, notation, and necessary assumptions.
Distinguish the mathematical object from its representation, estimate, or implementation.
Define essential prerequisites briefly here and link to substantial supporting notes.
Replace these generic headings with topic-specific level-two sections.
For example, an Autoencoders note can have Autoencoders, VAE, and Conditional VAE sections.
Give important sections stable IDs such as {#vae} for links from other pages.
-->

<!-- Short supporting definitions
Pastel-highlighted terms show a definition on hover, keyboard focus, or tap.
Add a reusable entry in notes/study-notes/_glossary.yml, then write:
[random variable]{.term key="random-variable"}
Use the displayed wording that fits the sentence; the key selects the definition.
For a context-specific reminder, override the text:
[parameter]{.term key="parameter" definition="Here, a learned weight or bias held fixed during prediction."}
An optional href attribute overrides the glossary's link to a full source note.
Use root-relative source links such as /notes/study-notes/mathematics/probability.qmd.
Keep definitions to one or two plain-text sentences; put equations in the main explanation.
Annotate useful first occurrences, not every repetition, heading, equation, code span, or existing link.
The main definition and any assumption required to understand a result must remain visible.
Without JavaScript or when printed, the short definitions are included inline.
For non-HTML exports, they become footnotes.
-->

-->
